attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Faithful. 'These systems' in context means generative AI. Firm and unhedged, but 'stable' is vague and rhetorical.

contract.note: The plain reading (reliably coherent and dependable in ordinary use) is ordinary. The support and contradiction conditions are balanced. The result still turns on an unstated threshold.

evidence.note: GPT-4 report from before the post admits it is not fully reliable. That is one model's imperfect reliability, not proof that the class was never stable.
OpenAI's own statement that normal operation was restored after one incident. It is not longitudinal evidence of stability either way.

reviews.rationale: Neither item meets either condition. e1 shows known reliability limits and e2 shows recovery from one incident. Neither shows class-wide perpetual instability or sustained stable operation. The packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful, reading 'around then' as a typo for 'around them'. Universal, firm historical claim.

contract.note: The contract counts any narrow conditional certificate as a 'safety guarantee'. Here that is a bound against adversarial token additions, and it only holds if the base filter already flags the harmful prompt. An informed reader would take Marcus to mean meaningful assurance that the systems behave safely. That reading is stretched against him, and it alone decides the result.

evidence.note: Erase-and-check (Feb 12, 2024) proves a bound that depends on the filter being right. It would contradict only under the contract's broad reading. Under the ordinary reading it is a robustness certificate, not a guarantee that the system is safe.
Independent critique (Oct 2023) bypassed the defense outside its assumptions. This shows how limited the guarantee is in practice.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's reading, e1 would contradict the claim. That reading is stretched, so I mark the contract unfair. Under the ordinary reading, no item shows a meaningful safety guarantee for generative AI before publication, and no item comprehensively shows none existed. The outcome stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. The garbled phrasing still clearly asserts that people were reporting problems.

semantics.note: Faithful. Keeps 'people', 'a variety of problems' and the 'last few hours' window.

contract.note: Fair, ordinary reading: multiple people reporting different ChatGPT problems around Feb 20–21. The contract says the post has no time, but it has one (02:32Z); this does not affect the result.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own status page, Feb 20, says it is investigating reports of unexpected responses. Corroborates that the reports existed.
Original user report, Feb 20 at 11:39pm: language mixing and wrong answers. The user says others had the same problem.
A separate user, Feb 20 at 11:54pm, reports incoherent output, and another user confirms. A different symptom from e2.

reviews.rationale: Several users posted reports on Feb 20 describing different ChatGPT problems (language mixing, wrong answers, gibberish). OpenAI's incident record corroborates them, all within hours of the post. The support condition is met.
